      "id": "houserules.glob-union-matcher",
      "kind": "gotcha",
      "area": "template",
      "summary": "globMatch in tools/kb.mjs is a union: matchesGlob for the full vocabulary, globToRegExp only for `**`/`*` with dot-segments; combining both matches neither.",
      "body": [
        "node:path matchesGlob excludes a path segment that starts with `.` under `**` (undocumented; verified live on Node 24.18.1). globToRegExp restores dot-segments but translates only `**` and `*`, escaping every other metacharacter as a literal.",
        "Write area and check globs with `**`, `*`, and literals only. Extend globToRegExp first if a glob ever needs `?`, `[ ]`, or `{ }` to cross a dot-segment; a mismatch is silent — the file simply drops out of the audit package.",
        "When replacing a matching engine, pin the old engine's full vocabulary with counterexample tests before switching call sites (batch 6 task 1 round 1)."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "globs",
        "audit",
        "areas"
      ],
      "source": {
        "date": "2026-09-02",
        "by": "review",
        "ref": "batch 6 branch review; task 1 review round 0"
      },
      "verify": [
        "tools/kb.mjs"
      ],
      "topic": "houserules"
    },
    {
      "id": "houserules.node-under-mise",
      "kind": "gotcha",
      "area": "global",
      "summary": "`node` and `pnpm` are on PATH only under `mise exec --` or `mise run` (`mise exec -- pnpm test`); without `mise.toml`, mise resolves no tools.",
      "body": [
        "For a scratch directory, run tools as `mise x node@24.18.1 pnpm@11.18.0 -- <command>`; mise strips the paths of inactive tools, so a PATH export does not survive `mise x`.",
        "The shipped wrappers `tools/kb.sh` and `tools/backlog.sh` use `node` from PATH and fall back to `mise exec node` on their own."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "mise",
        "node",
        "environment"
      ],
      "source": {
        "date": "2026-08-31",
        "by": "controller",
        "ref": "session of 2026-08-31: mise could not exec npm in a scratch directory; probe of 2026-09-01"
      },
      "topic": "houserules"
    },

      "id": "houserules.release-please-schema-gap",
      "kind": "gotcha",
      "area": "global",
      "summary": "release-please's config JSON schema omits prerelease-type and skip-snapshot from its root; keep those settings under packages['.'].",
      "body": [
        "The schema at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/googleapis/release-please/v17.11.2/schemas/config.json sets `additionalProperties: false` on the config root. The root's own `properties` list omits `prerelease-type` and `skip-snapshot`. `src/manifest.ts` reads both at the top level, like `versioning` and `release-type`. The project's docs show a top-level example with `prerelease-type`. The omission is a gap in the schema, not the runtime.",
        "Verified with `ajv-cli validate`. A root-level `prerelease-type` key fails with `params.additionalProperty: 'prerelease-type'` (`must NOT have additional properties`). The identical key nested under `packages['.']` validates cleanly: that path's value schema (`ReleaserConfigOptions`, reached through `allOf`) carries no such restriction.",
        "Put `prerelease-type`, `skip-snapshot`, and the other release settings under `packages['.']` in `release-please-config.json`, not at the config root. `src/manifest.ts` merges each package's config over the root default per key, so a single-package repository behaves identically either way. Only the nested placement passes the schema the file's own `$schema` points at."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "release-please",
        "schema",
        "config"
      ],
      "source": {
        "date": "2026-09-03",
        "by": "review",
        "ref": "batch 11 task 3 review, finding 3"
      },
      "verify": [
        "release-please-config.json"
      ],
      "topic": "houserules"
    },

      "id": "quality.no-compat-softening",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Never soften a design for backward compatibility. Make the correct change and migrate everything it breaks; the codebase is not built on compromises.",
      "body": [
        "When a better contract, field, or shape exists, adopt it and update every consumer, fixture, report, and document in the same change.",
        "Do not keep a deprecated field, alias, fallback, or optional-for-compat setting alive for old callers; the migration is part of the change, not a later batch.",
        "A genuinely optional concept stays optional on its merits; optionality is never a compatibility device."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "quality",
        "compatibility"
      ],
      "source": {

    {
      "id": "quality.principles",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "YAGNI, KISS, DRY; prefer a well-maintained library to custom code; one responsibility per unit; tests assert behavior; a11y and i18n are part of done.",
      "body": [
        "YAGNI: build only what the current backlog item needs.",
        "KISS: choose the simplest design that meets the requirement. No abstraction for one caller, no option without a second use, no layer that only forwards.",
        "DRY once logic has two real call sites: never leave a copy that can drift (shared constants, option factories, one write path). One call site is not yet duplication.",
        "Prefer a well-maintained library (vetted, exact-pinned) to a custom implementation of a solved problem: parsing, validation, globbing, dates, retries. A standing project decision may rule an exception; record it as an entry.",
        "One responsibility per file and per function. Each unit boundary is one a reader can understand without its internals.",
        "Tests assert behavior, not implementation details, and can fail. Clean up global and module state (mocks, prototypes) after each test.",
        "A dedicated compliance pass over the existing codebase is its own backlog item; new code complies immediately.",
        "Tests assert behavior, not implementation details, and can fail. Clean up global and module state (mocks, prototypes) after each test; an auto-restore setting covers only spies, so a mock created in a module-mock factory gets its own explicit afterEach reset."
      ],
      "tags": [
        "quality"
      ],

      "id": "security-hygiene.exact-pins",

      "summary": "Pin exact versions. Install only with a CLI (`pnpm add --save-exact`, `cargo add <crate>@=<version>`). Never write a version number by hand.",
      "body": [
        "Ranges (`^`, `~`) widen the attack surface. Resolve to the latest stable version at install time.",
        "The deterministic check covers `package.json`; ranges inside the `engines` object are floors, not dependency pins, and are exempt. Other ecosystems are judged by the reviewer under the same rule."

      "id": "writing-style.doc-comments",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Document every exported symbol with the language's doc-comment convention. Name things so the code reads without comments.",
      "body": [
        "A doc comment states what the item is for, its invariants, and what it returns or raises when the signature does not say so. It never restates the signature.",
        "Conventions: TSDoc in TypeScript, JSDoc in JavaScript, rustdoc in Rust, docstrings in Python — the language's standard form.",
        "Self-documenting code first: full words, verbs for functions, `is`/`has` for booleans, no abbreviation a newcomer must decode, one meaning per name. A comment that explains a name means the name is wrong.",
        "Comments inside a body still follow writing-style.code-comments: only for a constraint the code cannot show."

      "id": "writing-style.principles",
      "kind": "rule",
      "area": "global",
      "standing": true,
      "summary": "Write docs, comments, commit messages, and reports in ASD-STE100 style: short sentences, active voice, one instruction per sentence, concise.",
      "body": [
        "Sources: Williams, *Style*; Gopen & Swan, \"The Science of Scientific Writing\". They apply on top of ASD-STE100.",
        "Make the main character the subject and its action the verb.",
        "Unpack nominalizations into verbs: \"perform validation of\" becomes \"validate\".",
        "Delete expletives (\"there is\", \"it is\"), filler (\"in order to\", \"the fact that\", \"note that\"), and hedges that carry no information.",
        "Put old information in the topic position, new information in the stress position.",
        "Keep subject and verb adjacent.",
        "End on the emphasis."
      ],
